samples.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small cassette drawn with a thick black frame, and every pale grey mark lying outside that frame is inert decoration that means nothing. Inside the frame there are two pale beds. The upper bed is a tray of nine equal square cells in three rows of three. Eight of those cells are filled with a solid colour: exactly two red, two green, two blue and two yellow. The ninth cell is left as bare pale bed, and that cell is the gap. One tray cell also carries a thick black ring drawn just inside its own border; the ring is only a marking and the cell it rings holds a colour like any other cell. The lower bed is a strip of four equal slots, each holding one solid black arrow, and the four arrows are carried out in order from the leftmost slot to the rightmost slot. Each arrow points up, down, left or right, and it says which way the gap moves for that step: the gap exchanges places with the single coloured cell immediately next to it in the direction the arrow points, so that cell's colour slides into the square the gap has just left and the gap takes over that cell. Every one of the four arrows shown is a move the gap can actually make, so the gap never runs off the tray, and nothing else in the tray changes during a step. The ring never moves: it stays on the same tray cell from the first step to the last, and only the colours slide. After all four arrows have been carried out, which colour stands in the ringed cell? Answer with one of red, green, blue or yellow.
